subject: Immediate executive attention: CargoNest inference degradation after modelpack-2028V3 rollout
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cargonest.com>

Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@cargonest.com>, CargoNest SRE <sre@cargonest.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Severe slowdown & errors after modelpack-2028V3 rollout

Hi Jasmine,

We pushed the new modelpack-2028V3 on your hosted endpoint this morning (per the canary green from CI) and within ~30 minutes we started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency and a growing stream of 5xx errors for our high-throughput shipping label generation route. Key metrics from our side:
- p99 latency jumped from ~320ms to ~980ms for the route (tokens per request similar)
- 5xx rate increased from 0.2% to ~3.8%
- throughput dropped ~40% during peak windows (requests throttled by timeout)

We're blocked on peak-hour routing; this is impacting customer SLA commitments. We attached a short CSV with percentiles and a zip of recent ops logs. Can your team advise rollback or immediate mitigations? This is causing incident calls here.

Please escalate — we need an ETA for either a rollback to the previous modelpack or an urgent mitigations plan.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of ML Ops
CargoNest

Attachments: cargonest_latency_snapshot_20280312.csv, ops_logs_03-12.zip

Subject: Re: Severe slowdown & errors after modelpack-2028V3 rollout

Hi Elena — thank you for the detail and the logs. I'm escalating immediately.

Quick notes from initial glance: early signs point to a quantization-selection path in modelpack-2028V3 where a newer 4-bit execution kernel is being used for batches over 128 tokens; we've seen similar p99 regressions in internal perf testing on certain NVL arrays when mixed batching spikes occur.

I'm looping in Product and Runtime (Irene, Rishi, Priyom). We'll confirm rollback feasibility and provide an action plan in the next 30–60 minutes. If you have a sample request id that reproduces a 5xx, please paste it here; that'll speed triage.

— Jasmine

Subject: Fwd: Severe slowdown & errors after modelpack-2028V3 rollout — immediate triage + rollback options

Team — taking point on runtime triage. Summary of our findings after a 15m drill:
- Reproduced p99 spike on a canary VM using the same traffic pattern (high-concurrency bursts with mixed short/long sequences).
- Root cause hypothesis: the modelpack introduced an updated qprofile that flips certain layers to a new fast4 kernel which is heat-sensitive on our vGPU scheduling path; under concurrent KV cache thrash the kernel stalls and triggers request timeouts.
- Secondary: an unguarded fallback path for the decoder when the KV cache mismatch occurs emits a 5xx (decode error) rather than graceful degrade.

Immediate mitigations we can take within 30–60m:
1) Controlled rollback of modelpack-2028V3 to modelpack-2028V2 on the CargoNest tenant (fastest path).
2) Apply a temporary routing rule: route CargoNest high-QPS routes to the compatible v2 variant (model variant id: cargo-v2-stable) — requires a config flip, no binary redeploy.
3) Deploy a hotfix to change the kernel-selection heuristic to avoid fast4 for mixed bursts (estimated 3–4 hours).

Recommendation: perform option (1) now for immediate SLA recovery and option (3) for long-term fixes.

Irene
VP, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference

Attachments: modelpack-2028V3-config-diff.txt (config diff showing qprofile changes)

Elena — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What we did: 
- At 09:20 PDT on 2028-03-12 we flipped CargoNest tenant routing to cargo-v2-stable (targeted tenant rollback).
- Observed recovery within 6 minutes: p99 reverted to ~340ms and 5xx fell back to 0.3%. Throughput recovered to baseline.
- Attached: ops_logs_03-12.zip contains request ids showing the rollback window; modelpack-2028V3-config-diff.txt highlights the qprofile changes responsible.

Next steps (per Irene/Rishi):
- Internal: full postmortem and kernel-selection fix (ETA 4 hours for draft, 48 hours for permanent fix).
- Customer: we're opening a formal incident (SUP-4521) and will share the PM postmortem and mitigation timeline.
- Credits: Rishi will propose service credits; we will include a detailed timeline and mitigation report.

Please let me know if you'd like an exec-to-exec call today; happy to set that up. Again, deeply sorry for the impact — our priority is to restore confidence and avoid recurrence.

— Jasmine
